facts.title: Discovery and alternative activation
facts.fact: Ordinary discovery scans PBS root *.txt only, matches exact base or base_ suffix after longest-base ordering. Gen5–8 subdirectories are author alternatives, not simultaneous or automatically active registries. Explicit facility Trainers/Pokemon paths bypass generic basename discovery. A copied backup remains subject to current schema, dependencies, code and settings; changing its directory name does not recompute loaded settings constants.

facts.title: Lexical and schema collection
facts.fact: First-line BOM removal, physical comment/blank skip and subsequent first-# suffix deletion precede ordinary attribute collection. A space followed by # within ordinary section becomes invalid empty attribute, unlike specialized prepped-line loops. Ordinary repeated attributes overwrite; ^ fields accumulate; valid unknown schema attributes are ignored. Fixed schema ignores excess tail, q consumes preprocessed original string. Escaped-quote marker removal is positional; ordinary CSV quotation is not a general unquote guarantee.

facts.title: Registry identity and incomplete compile
facts.fact: String IDs normalize to Symbol, comparisons and enum membership are exact; no STICK→LEEK or VICEGRIP→VISEGRIP alias is supplied by generic registry. get unknown raises; try_get unknown/nil returns nil, but wrong types fail validation. Direct register replaces same key; ordinary compiler duplicate gate rejects before second registration. Clear and successful prefix registrations occur before whole-table validation/save. Failure does not itself undo earlier in-memory registrations.

facts.title: Four schema families and defaults
facts.fact: Each actual author field is parsed by its declared schema. Type references and Move Type/Target and Item Move are validated against the current registered dependency, not the English display label. Missing and explicit zero/false remain distinct. All complete defaults and field interpretations are in field-contracts.json; every present and omitted field of all 7704 primary path-records binds that contract in record-field-ledger.json.

facts.title: Move validation and effect identity
facts.fact: Status with positive power rejects before current record registration; Physical/Special with zero or omitted power warns and becomes Status. FunctionCode is author text and is not validated against a move-effect implementation at compile time. Factory resolves exact function name (digit prefix Effect); lawful absent effect falls back to Unimplemented. Missing/nil function uses None, not arbitrary empty or malformed name. Source and formal lawful missing-effect examples already preserve different status-failure and ordinary-damage branches.

facts.title: Types, generation and combat categories
facts.fact: All default19 and Gen5 18 rows read; Gen6/7/8 equal default. QMARKS is pseudo and neutral in supplied table, not universally unusable. Gen5 lacks FAIRY and retains STEEL resistance to DARK/GHOST. Each defending type checks weaknesses before resistances before immunities; generic Effectiveness.calculate multiplies all supplied defending arguments without deduplication, while ordinary battler type collection supplies its own deduplicated types. Per-move category switch is independent of author backup; old-category mode queries current type special flag. Optional Shadow input is a separate activation condition.

facts.title: Ability data versus callback behavior
facts.fact: All1122 per-path ability records bind ID/name/description/Flags. Data descriptions are display strings; callback lookup uses effective ability identity at each actual caller. FasterEggHatching is present only on the explicitly read flagged rows (MAGMAARMOR/FLAMEBODY, plus default/Gen8 STEAMENGINE). Neither a plain description nor registration proves handler activation. MERCILESS reads target poison; wording it poisoned is not a source admission rule. Gen5/6/7 availability164/191/233 and current267 do not imply mechanic-generation changes.
formal_receivers: received WP48/WP49 finite source families and AB vectors

facts.title: Every move field and dynamic consumers
facts.fact: All3333 per-path move records bind Type/Category/Power/Accuracy/PP/Target/Priority/EffectChance/Flags and exact FunctionCode to the complete named move family contributions. Power1 can be a variable-power marker; accuracy0 has its own bypass; zero total PP is not finite exhaustion. Source target metadata distinguishes num_targets from final list length, User0 from failure, dynamic target replacement, range and foe-side flags. Actual common target/PP/ability/status guards remain before or after family-specific hooks; description order is not execution order.

facts.title: Alternative move differences
facts.fact: All four unique move payloads were actually read. Old VICEGRIP identity becomes default VISEGRIP; Gen5 SheerCold OHKO differs from later OHKOIce; Gen5 DarkVoid SleepTarget differs from later user-Darkrai gate and Gen7+ accuracy50; Gen5 HiddenPower author power1 versus later60 is separate from old-mechanic power function. Gen5–7 Teleport FleeFromBattle differs from default SwitchOutUserStatusMove priority−6. All other exact changed fields and availability bind the same per-field contracts, not a blanket legacy-mechanics claim.

facts.fact: CRE-B actually full-read four unique primary item payloads2457 records and associated Gen8/default693; received3150 primary path-records plus separately Shadow4. facts.title: Fling and NaturalGift current identity
facts.fact: Current berry and any NaturalGift prefix admit that family; complete type+digits and complete power matching have separate fallbacks. Gen5 raw60/70/80 differs from later80/90/100. Fling requires active losable current item and its own berry-consumption gate, with prefix admission distinct from numeric power. Per-hit current identity and later actual current-item consumption are not frozen at selection. Existing NG self-consumption and Fling InnardsOut→ORAN missing-item failure prefixes, controls, no rollback and unexecuted status were actually received.

facts.title: Facility list graph and compile behavior
facts.fact: Exactly five list sections. Default references Tower; pokecupsingle/double→Poke, little→Little, pika→Pika, fancycupsingle/double→Fancy_single. The alternative Fancy618 has no current list selector. compile_trainer_lists stores trainer/template arrays, names, filenames and default bit; missing referred files become empty arrays. Challenges on Default are skipped. Loader rescues list load failure to [] and searches matching nondefault then firstdefault. No general all-files/all-items registration or list nonemptiness guarantee.

facts.title: Facility template normalization
facts.fact: Template species/item/nature use permissive existence checks. Unknown item becomes nil; unknown moves drop and valid moves compress among first MAX_MOVES; only all-invalid falls back to first Move.keys (default MEGAHORN). EV names are fixed recognized aliases and unrecognized are ignored. Creation uses a new Pokemon without default moves, assigns actual item (no can_hold gate), chosen nature/happiness0, move objects, IV allstats and integer EV_LIMIT/number-of-EV-stats before recalculation. RETURN→FRUSTRATION is conditional on registry existence at creation.

facts.title: Tower missing literal controls
facts.fact: Named PBF actual reader reports882 Tower templates/1600 trainers and full references: only84 raw item IDs has STICK unknown at physical line140/index137, hence nil under current registry; LEEK is different. Only330 raw move IDs has VICEGRIP unknown line252/index249, leaving BUBBLEBEAM/KNOCKOFF/PROTECT. Every actual Tower row retains at least one valid move, so fallback is unreachable in this finite table. ItemClause ignores nil and compares actual identity; no need to assert all authored literals register. This is a bounded received table fact plus own exact parser, not personal raw Tower reading.
source_units: received PBF-ITEM/PBF-MOVE/PBF trait and CSV contracts

facts.title: Facility eligibility and consumption boundary
facts.fact: Actual PBF/FAC receipts preserve template pool/trait/party constraints, fancyboth single file selection, infeasible ordinary factory level totals and unbounded rejection loops. Filename/record existence does not prove eligibility or termination. Organized battle item snapshots follow heal/adjustment and normal positional restoration; exceptions do not guarantee restoration. These finite named consumer facts are received, without granting all facility formal/shared catalog/history completion.

facts.title: Compile, save, startup reload and failure
facts.fact: Main loads core messages, plugins, Compiler.main, then Game.initialize. Compiler.main is debug-gated, uses missing required data/full flag/CTRL/import and integer-second maximum text>=maximum data time trigger; deletes listed data before full stage if triggered. Types→abilities→moves→items precede dependent species/trainers/facilities. Direct full-content entry lacks startup discovery decision/predelete/rescue. Reset/SystemExit rethrow; other diagnosed failures attempt listed deletion, not guaranteed transaction. Successful stage saves table/message outputs; ordinary startup GameData.load_all replaces registries. No Ruby/serialized load was run here.

facts.title: Existing objects and save-game reload
facts.fact: Game.load(save_data) applies saved values/maps rather than recompiling or calling GameData.load_all. Pokemon::Move holds ID/PP/PPUp but queries data fields and totalPP live by ID. Battle::Move snapshots name/function/power/type/category/accuracy/target/priority/effectChance and clones flags at construction; its totalPP may delegate to realMove unless positive explicit override. AIMove wraps this existing battle object, sets calcType and moldBreaker during setup and uses skill-dependent own handlers/callbacks. Registry reload cannot be generalized to refresh all existing battle snapshots, caches or old data instances.

facts.title: Writer and language/resource boundaries
facts.fact: Generic writer selects suffix paths from current registry entries, emits BOM/CRLF and schema properties. Type/Ability/Move/Item omissions use constructor/default/property policies; Item false Consumable for nonimportant must be written, sale-half/BP1/use0 may omit. Facility writer exports normalized arrays and strict present move identities. Display names/descriptions use message-domain lookup; icon resolver can fall back and depends on real resource existence. Author text and metadata do not prove translated text, pixels, host availability or byte round-trip.

facts.title: AI differences and real combat
facts.fact: AIMove unconditionally substitutes basepower1→60 before its medium-skill gate; only the optional AI basepower handler depends on that gate. Its rough type/priority/damage/accuracy/critical queries can invoke actual callback writes and explicit untriggering, but do not reproduce all true use ordering or RNG. Data Target/Function/PP/flags and current ability/item identity are distinct inputs. AI own OHKOIce ice gate does not restore actual loaded-clause target gate. Conversion User0 generic score path and separately defined target-handler remain distinct; root-owned AI001 is not duplicated.
